title_plain: Bull edges Round 3 by fixing the exit, but the reward is still modest
summary_plain: Bull listened to the Judge and moved the safety exit from $14 away to $21 away, about one normal hour of price wiggle. That makes the trade fairer, but it pays only about $1.70 for each $1 risked if both targets are reached. Bear made good points: the price is still under every average line, trading is very thin, and the first target is a spot where sellers have shown up. But Bear attacked the old $14 exit, which Bull had already dropped, so part of Bear's closing missed.

best_point_plain.bull: Bull widened the exit to a sensible size and admitted honestly that the trade only pays well if the bounce keeps going past the first target.
best_point_plain.bear: Ether is still below all its important average lines, the hourly selling push is still strong, and trading is so thin that a climb to the $2,096 ceiling is shaky.

checks.claim: 1h ATR14 19.86, so stop 2047 (21 below 2068) is about 1.06x 1h ATR
checks.note_plain: My fresh check shows a normal one-hour swing of about $20 (19.96). A $21 exit is about one normal swing, so it is a fair size now.

checks.claim: Next 7 five-minute candles after the flush had lows no lower than about 2061; none went back toward 2028
checks.note_plain: The 24-hour low is still $2,028.32, so nothing has gone back there. The little floor near $2,061 is about 35 minutes old, which is still young.
The math is right. But the first target alone pays only 1.3 for 1, so most of the reward depends on reaching the second target.

checks.claim: Bull's stop is 14 points, about 0.7x the 1h ATR of 19.86
checks.note_plain: True for the old $2,054 exit, but Bull's final plan uses $2,047 ($21). Bear wrote at the same time and could not see the change.

checks.claim: Volume 0.12x (5m) and 0.07x (15m) of normal; price under SMA50/SMA200 on all charts
checks.note_plain: My check shows trading even thinner (0.17x on 5 minutes, 0.1x on 15 minutes, 0.05x on the hour), and price is under every long-term average.

checks.claim: 1h MACD histogram -3.78 vs -3.08 before, selling push still growing
checks.note_plain: Matches: now -3.74 vs -3.08. The push is still growing on the hourly chart, though it is easing on the 5-minute chart.

checks.claim: US Ether funds lost $271.9M Nov 2-5; first target 2096 equals session VWAP
checks.note_plain: The target really is the day's average price (2095.9). Bear says it opened the fund report and the four days add up; the exact size is still debated by other sites, but the direction is outflows.

watch_next_plain: The Judge now decides: is a trade that risks $21 to win about $28 to $45 on thin trading, against a downtrend, good enough, and has any big news event been missed?
